post.caption:
Salting, drying, smoking, fermenting and sugar preservation all do the same job by different routes: make the food a place microbes cannot work. Canning was invented to win a prize Napoleon offered for feeding an army on the move. Refrigeration came last and rewrote what a city could eat. Every method buys the same thing, which is time. And a surplus that keeps is exactly what allows anyone to stop producing food and do something else.
